title: Investigation lifecycle checklist — rollforward debugging (working)
content:
Purpose:
A compact, checklist-style guide for incident investigators who need to perform a rollforward (continue with a mitigation/fallback or switch model variant) rather than an immediate rollback. Focus is on fast signal collection, safe rollforward gating, and evidence capture for post-incident analysis. This is intentionally lightweight — intended to be kept as a Drive working doc (notes, snippets, incomplete items) rather than a formal runbook.

Scope and when to prefer rollforward:
- Rollforward: when a partial mitigation (fallback model, degraded-quality but higher-availability variant, or traffic shaping) can keep customer-facing latency/availability within SLA and reduces blast radius compared to rollback.
- Rollback: prefer when the new change is clearly the root cause and previous version is known-good with no downstream incompatibilities.
- Use this checklist when (a) model rollouts, quantized runtimes, or routing-policy changes cause sudden regressions, or (b) traffic surges break autoscaling/queueing and a capacity-tier fallback could stabilize user experience.

Quick hypothesis triage (first 8 minutes):
- Confirm scope: percentage of traffic affected, tenant list, region, and route. Query: tenant-weighted error/latency for last 5m.
- Isolate change window: correlate to deployments/rollout events (canary start times, model version pin, quantization toggle).
- Simple guard rails: did rate-limits/quotas/tracing-sampling change? Look at recent feature-flag toggles.
- Evidence capture: snapshot 5–10 representative traces (span-level), 20 random prompts from failures for prompt-replay. Save to incident gist/paste.

Signals to gather (minimal set — reduce noise):
1) High-level metrics (single numbers, 1-line queries):
  - p50/p90/p99 latency per route (last 5m vs baseline 1h).
  - error rate (5xx, model timeouts, grpc errors) by tenant.
  - CPU/GPU utilization and queue length for pools serving the model variant.
  - KV cache hit-rate and eviction rate for affected model pool.
  - Token-per-request distribution shift (are prompts suddenly much longer?).
2) Trace anchors to grab immediately:
  - RPC entry span -> model selection span -> runtime-exec span -> kvcache span -> response serializing span.
  - For each trace, annotate: tenant_id, model_version, route, backend_node_id.
3) Lightweight artifact collection:
  - 10 trace ids with full spans.
  - 5 example prompts + model responses (redact PHI).
  - Snapshot of autoscaler decisions and pod/node events in last 30m.

Dashboard slices to open first (fastest to read):
- Route overview panel: stacked p50/p90/p99 microtiles, delta vs baseline.
- Tenant anomaly list: top 10 deviating tenants by delta-p99.
- Pool health: per-GPU queue length + oom/killed pods.
- Kv-warmth mini-heatmap: hit-rate over last 30m by tenant.
- Fallback routing path counter: how many requests hit fallback variants.
- Sampling of trace-based latencies: median span durations for model-exec and kvcache.
Note: Keep only 6 panels open on operator screen to reduce cognitive load.

Decision gating for rollforward (binary checklist):
- Does rollback create unacceptable client-visible failures? (Y/N)
- Can we safely route subset of traffic to a fallback variant that is compatible? (Y/N)
- Is there an automated canary gate we can use (traffic % ramp step) to test rollback alternative? (Y/N)
- Is cost of mitigation acceptable (e.g., extra GPU allocation, slower model)? (Y/N)
If majority are Y and risk is limited -> proceed with controlled rollforward.

Controlled rollforward steps (operator-facing, order matters):
1) Notify stakeholders: post to incident channel, include brief summary and planned traffic change.
2) Snapshot baseline metrics (store query results and a screenshot).
3) Create small-scale rollforward: route 5–10% traffic to fallback variant or enable the degraded-path flag.
4) Observe for 3–5 minutes: check p99, error-rate, KV-hit. If improvement -> ramp to 25%, then 50% with 5–10m observation windows.
5) If any critical signal worsens (30% increase in p99 for customer-facing tenants or rise in 5xx), abort ramp and revert routing.
6) If stable at 50% after one hour, schedule final cutover or follow up with engineering to root cause while mitigation remains.

Runbook query snippets (plain text to paste into dashboards/console):
- latency delta (example): SELECT quantile(0.99, latency_ms) FROM token_path WHERE route = 'chat' AND ts > now() - 5m GROUP BY tenant_id
- kv hit rate: SELECT sum(kv_hits)/sum(kv_lookups) FROM model_pool_metrics WHERE pool = 'g4x-ams' AND ts > now() - 30m
- trace sample: trace_id IN (SELECT trace_id FROM spans WHERE service='runtime' AND span_name='model.exec' AND duration_ms > 200 ORDER BY duration_ms DESC LIMIT 10)
(put these snippets into incident paste for reproducibility)

Communication & handoff notes:
- Short term: update incident-channel every 15 minutes during ramp. Use header: [Rollforward] % traffic -> variant-X ; p99 delta ; top-3 affected tenants.
- Engineering on-call: create GitHub issue with collected artifacts and assign to model-runtime lead.
- Post-handoff: leave mitigation in place until a planned maintenance window unless rollback needed.

Post-incident capture (must-do before closing):
- Timeline: record exact timestamps for observed regression start, mitigation actions, and when signals returned to baseline.
- Save artifacts: traces, example prompts, dashboard screenshots, routing config, autoscaler logs. Put all into incident folder and link to ticket.
- Root cause hypothesis: 1–2 sentence summary and next action with owner (e.g., "KV eviction spike due to TTL change; investigate TTL config drift - owner: Diego Ramos").
- Lessons & preventive work: propose a follow-up ticket for (a) additional smoke probes for kv-warmth, (b) traffic-shaping policy tests, (c) automating small-scale rollforward ramp.

Investigation anti-patterns (avoid these):
- Opening 20 dashboards at once and trying to correlate visually. Open focused slices only.
- Relying on a single trace sample. Always gather a small set across tenants/nodes.
- Making large traffic changes without a defined abort threshold and observation window.

Open questions / TODOs (working):
- How to standardize a 1-click snapshot of the 6 core panels for incident evidence? (owner: Maya)
- Add a 'rollforward-safe' label to model catalog entries for quick gating (owner: product-hosted-api)
- Shorten telemetry collection latency for kvcache metrics from 60s to 15s for faster gating (owner: infra)

References and related docs:
- CONFLUENCE-OBS-287: Investigations playbook (long-form)
- GH-PR-1423: autoscaler change log (deploy 2025-02-17)

Notes to self: keep this doc small, operator-centric. This is intentionally opinionated: rollforward is not default but exists for cases where rollback produces higher customer impact. Save snippets into incident template for next time.
